defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: The Outliner lists Actors in the level, and the Content Browser lists assets.
A Blueprint class is the template, and each placed copy is an Actor.
Play In Editor makes you the player, and Simulate runs with no player.
Edits made to Actors during play are thrown away when you press Stop.
Dot u asset and dot u map files are binary, so text tools cannot merge them.
A collision pair gets the weaker of its two responses.
bookends.command: Give me short cases from building a small game in Unreal, one at a time, and ask which part of the editor or which rule each case needs. Use Outliner, Content Browser, Details panel, Play In Editor, Simulate, Eject, Blueprint class, Event Graph, Construction Script and collision preset. I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Wait for my answer before you give yours.
checks: Check: every case comes from building a game, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you used the exact term and ruled out its look-alike.
